title: A process queued behind a busy owner is stolen by an idle worker, so no work waits beside an idle worker
purpose: Written by hand by Artemis, beamr's lead, on 4 November 2026, when B-184's gate at c1c61695 hung on a B-181 test on two machines and Apollo's stress runs showed it hangs at the base too. A hanging test fails the gate, so beamr 0.22.0 cannot ship until it is fixed; and the hang is a real scheduling defect, not a flaky test. In production it is a process that waits behind a worker busy in a long or blocking slice while another worker sits idle, which is how liminal work can stall with capacity free.
task: Let an idle worker steal a busy owner's last queued process, and make sure it is woken to do so (R1). Write the rule into the composition spec and the CHANGELOG (R2). Ship it in beamr 0.22.0 with B-184, under that release's one gate.

requirements.title: An idle worker steals the last process queued behind an owner that is running a slice
requirements.spec: Behavioural, red first. Found while gating B-184 at c1c61695 (4 November 2026): scheduler::tickless_idle_tests::conditions::surplus_behind_a_blocked_owner_runs_on_the_idle_worker hung on the MacBook Air and on Tom's MacBook Pro. Run alone it hangs at B-184's base 08014fa7 as well (39 of 40 runs on Skull, Linux; 40 of 40 at c1c61695 on Dean's laptop), so it is older than B-184. Both stack samples agree: the test waits for the second of the pair to start (conditions.rs:82), worker 0 runs the first of the pair, which holds it in a native slice, and worker 1 is parked in live_park. The cause, read from the code at 08014fa7: RunQueue::steal_half_from (run_queue.rs:124) leaves a victim with one queued process alone, "so the owning thread keeps its last runnable process". Worker 0 drains its woken list, pushes both of the pair, and raises W23's surplus edge (park.rs:132); but when worker 0 pops the first and starts its slice before worker 1's steal reads the queue, the queue holds one, the steal takes nothing, worker 1 parks again, and no source raises another edge while worker 0 is inside the slice. The second process waits until the owner's slice ends; behind a native that blocks, or a long slice, that is indefinitely, with a worker idle beside it. THE SYSTEM SHALL let an idle worker steal a victim's last queued process while the victim's owner is running a process slice. Each worker SHALL publish that it is in a slice: a per-worker flag raised (SeqCst) before the slice starts and lowered when it returns. steal_half_from SHALL take max(1, len/2) from a victim whose owner is in a slice, and leave a victim of one alone only when its owner is not. So that the steal is reached, the owner SHALL raise a busy-owner edge: after raising its flag and a fence(SeqCst), if its own run queue is not empty and another worker is idle (B-181's idle count, read after the fence), it runs edge E (wake_edge). This is the owner's half of a Dekker pair with the idle worker, which raises the idle count, fences, then reads the flags as it steals: either the owner sees the idle worker and wakes it, or the idle worker sees the owner busy and steals. A steal of two or more is unchanged. No timer, poll or count decides any of it.
acceptance: Red first, at 08014fa7 and quoted: the hanging test run alone under cargo nextest run with --stress-count 40, hangs/runs per machine, on Dean's laptop and on Skull. A hang ends by nextest's slow-timeout terminate-after, which is the harness's ceiling, never the test's own wait.

Red first: a run_queue test in which a victim queue of one, whose owner's flag is raised, is stolen from (returns 1). The existing steal_from_single_item_queue_returns_nothing still passes with the flag lowered.

Red first: a scheduler test that drives the interleaving deterministically with the park hooks and test seams, no sleeps: the owner pops the first of the pair and enters its slice before the idle worker's steal, and the second still starts on the idle worker. At the base it does not start; the test ends on the loss detector or a down message, never on a timer.
With the code: the hanging test run alone, --stress-count 400, 0 hangs, on Dean's laptop and on Skull, quoted beside the base counts.
Drift injections, each quoted in the handback: with the busy-owner edge removed the deterministic test fails; with the steal rule reverted it fails.
B-181's tickless-idle suite and wake-rate bound unchanged and green: an idle scheduler still makes no timed wake.

requirements.title: The spec and the CHANGELOG say what changed
requirements.spec: Documentary. docs/EMBEDDER-COMPOSITION-SPEC.md §3.8.2 SHALL gain the steal rule and the busy-owner edge as a condition beside C1, saying which half of the Dekker pair each side holds and why a victim of one is stolen only from a busy owner. CHANGELOG.md, in the release that carries B-184 (beamr 0.22.0), SHALL say that a process queued behind a worker running a long or blocking slice now runs on an idle worker, where before it waited for that slice to end.
acceptance: The spec's new condition and the CHANGELOG line quoted in the handback.

boundaries: SHALL NOT end any wait by a timer, a poll or a fixed sleep, in code or in tests.
SHALL NOT change a steal from a victim of two or more, or B-181's wake sequence, idle count or surplus edge, except by adding the busy-owner edge beside them.
SHALL NOT add unsafe code, or a dependency without its licence and the reason in Cargo.toml.
SHALL NOT mark any test serial, ignored or skipped to make it pass; the hanging test is fixed by the code, never by changing what it asserts.
verification: This handwritten brief passes the design gate of this repository, judged by its parsed failures, never by its exit code.
Every red written and run before its code, and quoted against 08014fa7 in the handback.

The full gate legs (fmt, clippy pedantic with --all-targets, ast-grep, nextest, cargo test --doc) green on the exact final commit of beamr 0.22.0, judged from parsed output, with df and the swap line in START and END; no build lock of any kind (Tom, 4 November 2026, 04:03).
Four-heading handback (BLOCKED ON, CHANGED, FOUND, NOT CONFIRMED).
Released in beamr 0.22.0 with B-184; haematite then liminal move their pins the same day (Tom's rule 16).
